name: okc-dashboard
description: Make a virtual machine, set it up, snapshot it, throw it away.
//main: An app page, loaded from disk. That is what makes NW.js behave normally: the page gets node, and the SDK build gives it a right-click Inspect of its own. Served over http instead it would be a remote page, which gets neither -- which is why nothing here has to hand-write a context menu.
//chromium-args: Deliberately none. The previous version passed --disable-features=nw2, which selects the older window implementation -- and under it NW.js's own nw.Window shim throws 'getRoutingID is not a function' on every page load, and native confirm() silently returns false. Nothing here needs the flag, so it is gone and both of those go with it. If something ever does need it, expect that error back.

scripts.test: node test/generic-test.js && node test/window-test.js && node test/declared-test.js

//dependencies: None, and that is a property worth keeping rather than an accident. What this app uses beyond NW.js is checked in under vendors/ -- the Ace editor, xterm.js, marked and nanotar -- because a dependency resolved by a package manager is whatever the registry served the day somebody last installed it, and the same window on another machine is then not the same window. See vendors/README.md.
